subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Hostile Takeovers and Defenses
description: Learn Hostile Takeovers and Defenses in one minute.

hook.text: A company wants to buy yours. Your board says no. They buy shares from your shareholders directly.

buildup.text: Hostile takeovers bypass the board by making offers directly to shareholders to acquire control.

discovery.text: Boards use 'poison pills' — shareholder rights plans that dilute the hostile bidder's stake to block takeovers.

twist.text: Poison pills protect boards but may also entrench poor management that should be replaced.

climax.text: Takeover defenses protect independence but can also shield incompetence. The balance is delicate.

punchline.text: Protect the company. Or protect the board. Same tool.

quiz.question: What is a poison pill in corporate governance?
options: A defense that dilutes a hostile bidder's ownership stake
A penalty for board members who resign
